key_insight: A neural network learns parameter-dependent knot densities to move IGA mesh points by minimizing a residual-based a posteriori energy-error estimator.
engineering_relevance: This enables automated r-adaptivity that can place degrees of freedom where they matter most, improving accuracy for singularities, interfaces, and boundary layers at fixed mesh size.
method: Solve the PDE with standard conforming Galerkin isogeometric analysis.
Use a neural network to map each problem parameter to a knot-density function and relocate interior knots.
Minimize a differentiable residual loss built from element residuals, flux jumps, and Neumann boundary terms via reverse-mode autodiff.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports one- and two-dimensional numerical experiments showing improved accuracy and degree-of-freedom concentration near difficult solution features.
watch_item: The estimator is guaranteed reliable/efficient only for coercive problems on admissible meshes; beyond that, the loss is still usable but theoretical error control is weaker.
paper_title: Parametric Neural r-Adaptivity for Isogeometric Analysis via Residual Minimization
